### link_shader_nodes

*changes the scene*

Connect an output socket to an input socket.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | [Owner](#owner) | **required** | Whose shader node tree. world defaults to the scene's world. |
| `from_node` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `from_socket` | string ≤63 or integer 0..255 | **required** | Socket identifier, name or index |
| `to_node` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `to_socket` | string ≤63 or integer 0..255 | **required** | Socket identifier, name or index |

### unlink_shader_socket

*changes the scene*

Remove links going into an input socket.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | [Owner](#owner) | **required** | Whose shader node tree. world defaults to the scene's world. |
| `node` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `socket` | string ≤63 or integer 0..255 | **required** | Socket identifier, name or index |

### set_node_input

*changes the scene*

Set an unlinked input socket's value (colors are RGBA).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | [Owner](#owner) | **required** | Whose shader node tree. world defaults to the scene's world. |
| `node` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `socket` | string ≤63 or integer 0..255 | **required** | Socket identifier, name or index |
| `value` | scalar or array of scalars | **required** |  |

### set_node_image

*changes the scene*

Assign an image to an Image Texture or Environment Texture shader node (create the node with add_shader_node first). Works for any file or generated image, including external ones; movie/sequence/tiled/render images are refused.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owner` | [Owner](#owner) | **required** | Whose shader node tree. world defaults to the scene's world. |
| `node` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `image` | _NameOrNull | **required** | Image name, or null to clear |

## Transform and placement

Cursor, origins and world-space placement of whole objects.

### set_cursor

*changes the scene*

Move the 3D cursor (used by set_origin mode 'cursor'). Give at most one of location (world space) or to_object (or neither, to only rotate it). With to_object, 'to' picks the spot: 'origin' (default), 'bounds_center' (center of its evaluated bounding box) or 'median' (median of the evaluated mesh vertices; non-mesh objects use their origin). rotation_deg optionally sets the cursor rotation too. Returns the new cursor.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `rotation_deg` | number[3] -36000..36000 | none | Euler XYZ in degrees |
| `to_object` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `to` | `origin` \| `bounds_center` \| `median` | none |  |

### set_origin

*changes the scene*

Move object origins without moving the geometry in the world (like Object > Set Origin). mode: geometry_bounds / geometry_median (center of the geometry), center_of_mass_surface / center_of_mass_volume, cursor (the 3D cursor, see set_cursor), point (a world-space 'point', required for this mode and only there; the cursor is left as it was), or geometry_to_origin (moves the geometry onto the origin instead). MESH/CURVE/FONT/SURFACE only. Data shared by several objects is refused unless make_single_user=true. Returns each object's new world location.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects` | array[1..500] of string ≤63 | **required** |  |
| `mode` | `geometry_bounds` \| `geometry_median` \| `center_of_mass_surface` \| `center_of_mass_volume` \| `cursor` \| `point` \| `geometry_to_origin` | **required** |  |
| `point` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `make_single_user` | boolean | false |  |

### apply_transform

*changes the scene, destructive*

Bake the object transform into the geometry (like Ctrl+A): afterwards the chosen parts of location / rotation / scale are identity and the vertices carry them (vertex indices stay the same, positions change). Default applies rotation and scale. Negative scales are handled (normals stay outward). MESH/CURVE/FONT/SURFACE only; shared data is refused unless make_single_user=true. Returns each object's new transform.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects` | array[1..500] of string ≤63 | **required** |  |
| `location` | boolean | false |  |
| `rotation` | boolean | true |  |
| `scale` | boolean | true |  |
| `make_single_user` | boolean | false |  |

### align_objects

*changes the scene*

Move objects so their world-space bounding boxes (evaluated, so modifiers count) line up on the chosen axes: mode min / center / max matches that side of each box to the reference. relative_to: 'first' (default: objects[0], which stays put), 'world_origin', 'cursor', 'selection_bounds' (the box around all listed objects) or {"object": name} (an object that stays put; it is skipped if also listed). Any object type works; cameras, lights and empties count as a point at their origin. Returns each object's new world location.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects` | array[1..500] of string ≤63 | **required** |  |
| `axes` | array[1..3] of `x` \| `y` \| `z` | **required** |  |
| `mode` | `min` \| `center` \| `max` | **required** |  |
| `relative_to` | `first` \| `world_origin` \| `cursor` \| `selection_bounds` or object | `"first"` |  |
| `relative_to.object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |

### distribute_objects

*changes the scene*

Spread 3+ objects evenly along a world axis. The two extreme objects (by current box center on that axis) stay put and the ones between them are moved. mode 'centers' (default): equal distance between bounding-box centers; 'gaps': equal empty space between neighbouring bounding boxes (negative if they overlap). Returns the objects in their new order along the axis, with world locations.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects` | array[3..500] of string ≤63 | **required** |  |
| `axis` | `x` \| `y` \| `z` | **required** |  |
| `mode` | `centers` \| `gaps` | `"centers"` |  |

### snap_objects

*changes the scene*

Move objects' origins onto a snap target (rotation and scale are kept; world space; a parented object ends with that world location). to: {"grid": increment} rounds the world location to the grid; "cursor" (the 3D cursor); {"object": name, "target": ...} with target 'origin' (default), 'bounds_center' (center of its evaluated bounding box), 'nearest_vertex' or 'nearest_surface' (closest point on the evaluated mesh to each moved object's origin; these two need a MESH target). The target object must not be in 'objects'. Returns each object's new world location.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects` | array[1..500] of string ≤63 | **required** |  |
| `to` | object or `cursor` or object | **required** |  |
| `to.grid` | number 1e-06..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `to.object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `to.target` | `origin` \| `nearest_vertex` \| `nearest_surface` \| `bounds_center` | `"origin"` |  |

### drop_to_surface

*changes the scene*

Drop objects onto surfaces, like Blender's 'drop to floor'. Rays go along 'direction' (default [0,0,-1]) from the object's evaluated vertices (large meshes: an 8x8 grid on the bounding-box face that leads; non-mesh objects: their origin) against 'targets' (mesh names; default every visible mesh not being moved) and optionally the plane z=floor_z. The object moves along the direction by the smallest hit distance minus 'offset' (so it rests on the surface, leaving a gap of offset). align_to_normal first rotates it about its origin so its local +Z (up) lines up with the surface normal at the closest hit. An object with no hit at all makes the whole call fail with not_found and nothing moves. Returns, per object, the new world location, the distance moved and what it landed on.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `objects` | array[1..500] of string ≤63 | **required** |  |
| `direction` | number[3] -1..1 | `[0, 0, -1]` |  |
| `targets` | array[1..100] of string ≤63 | none |  |
| `floor_z` | number -1000000..1000000 | none |  |
| `offset` | number -1000000..1000000 | `0.0` |  |
| `align_to_normal` | boolean | false |  |

### look_at

*changes the scene*

Rotate an object so its track_axis (default local -Z, which is what cameras and spot lights look along) points at a world point or at another object's origin, keeping up_axis (default local Y) as upright as possible. Location and scale are unchanged. track_axis and up_axis must be different axes. Returns the object summary.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `target` | object or object | **required** |  |
| `target.object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `target.point` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ in scene units |
| `track_axis` | `-Z` \| `Z` \| `-X` \| `X` \| `-Y` \| `Y` | `"-Z"` |  |
| `up_axis` | `X` \| `Y` \| `Z` | `"Y"` |  |

## Mesh analysis and repair

### analyze_mesh

*read-only*

Check mesh topology: holes (with locations), non-manifold edges, bowtie vertices, loose geometry, inconsistent normals, shells, degenerate faces, self-intersections, and volume when closed. is_manifold is true only for a closed, consistently oriented surface.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `evaluated` | boolean | false | Analyze the result of the modifier stack instead of the base mesh |

### find_close_vertices

*read-only*

Pairs of vertices closer than `distance` that aren't already joined by an edge (by default only open-boundary vertices): candidates for merge_vertices.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `distance` | number 0..1 | **required** | World-space search radius |
| `boundary_only` | boolean | true |  |
| `max_pairs` | integer 1..5000 | `500` |  |

### get_boundary_loops

*read-only*

List every hole (open boundary) as an ordered loop of vertex indices with world positions. Use it to see where the mesh is open before stitching.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `max_loops` | integer 1..200 | `50` |  |
| `max_vertices_per_loop` | integer 3..2000 | `200` |  |

### get_mesh_elements

*read-only*

List mesh elements (vertices, edges or faces) chosen by a selector (default: all), with the indices the edit ops use. verts: index, co, normal; edges: index, verts, length, is_boundary, seam, sharp; faces: index, verts, center, normal, area, material_index. `total` is the number of matches, `counts` is [vertices, edges, faces] for the selector's expect_counts. Positions are in `space` (default world). Works in Edit mode too (reads the live edit mesh). An empty match is an empty list, not an error.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `domain` | `verts` \| `edges` \| `faces` | `"verts"` |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` |  |
| `offset` | integer 0..9999999 | `0` |  |
| `limit` | integer 1..2000 | `200` |  |

### repair_mesh

*changes the scene*

Clean up a mesh and report before/after analyze_mesh results. Filling caps each hole with one n-gon: it closes the surface, but can't recreate missing detail.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `merge_distance` | number 0..0.1 | `0.0001` | Weld vertices closer than this (0 = don't) |
| `dissolve_degenerate` | boolean | true |  |
| `remove_loose` | boolean | true | Delete vertices/edges that belong to no face |
| `fill_holes_max_sides` | integer 0..100000 | `0` | Cap holes bounded by up to this many edges with a new face (0 = don't fill) |
| `recalculate_normals` | boolean | true | Make face winding consistent, pointing outward |

### merge_vertices

*changes the scene*

Merge chosen vertex groups (e.g. the two sides of a crack) into single vertices. Indices refer to the mesh before this call.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `groups` | array[1..5000] of array[2..32] of integer 0..10000000 | **required** | Each group of vertex indices is merged into one vertex |
| `position` | `center` \| `first` | `"center"` |  |

### fill_hole

*changes the scene*

Fill the single hole whose boundary passes through `vertex`: one n-gon, or triangulated (better for non-flat holes).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `vertex` | integer 0..10000000 | **required** | Vertex index (changes after topology edits) |
| `method` | `triangles` \| `ngon` | `"triangles"` |  |

### remove_duplicate_faces

*changes the scene*

Where several faces use exactly the same vertices (e.g. two overlapping copies of a region after merge_vertices), keep one and delete the rest; then delete edges/vertices left without faces.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |

### delete_faces

*changes the scene*

Delete specific faces, identified by their vertices; edges and vertices left without faces are removed too.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `faces` | array[1..5000] of array[3..64] of integer 0..10000000 | **required** | Each face given by its vertex indices (any order) |

### create_face

*changes the scene*

Create one face from existing vertices (to close a small gap by hand). Refuses if it would make an edge shared by 3+ faces.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `vertices` | array[3..64] of integer 0..10000000 | **required** | Vertex indices in order around the new face |

## Mesh editing

Operate on a selector, in Object mode, through bmesh.

### extrude

*changes the scene*

Extrude selected elements, like Blender's E. mode: 'region' (faces; adjacent faces extrude together, side walls are made, the original faces are removed as in the interactive tool), 'individual_faces', 'edges' (edge-only extrude: new edge ring plus side faces) or 'verts' (a new vertex and edge per vertex). The selector is resolved in faces (region, individual_faces), edges or vertices. Move the new geometry with `distance` (along the normal: the region's area-weighted average face normal; each face's own normal for individual_faces; average vertex normal for edges; each vertex's own normal for verts) or with `vector` (+ `space`); give neither to extrude in place and then use transform_elements. Returns created {verts, edges, faces} indices (+ *_count), and cap_faces (the moved copies of the original faces) for the face modes, so you can chain extrude/inset/transform_elements.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `mode` | `region` \| `individual_faces` \| `edges` \| `verts` | `"region"` |  |
| `distance` | number -1000000..1000000 | none |  |
| `vector` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` |  |

### inset

*changes the scene*

Inset faces, like Blender's I: a smaller copy of each face (or of the whole region's outline when individual=false) surrounded by a rim of new faces. thickness is the inset distance, depth moves the inner faces along the normal (negative = into the mesh), even_offset keeps thickness constant around corners, outset grows instead of shrinks (region only). Lengths are in `space` (world needs uniform object scale). Returns created.faces = the inner faces (they keep the input faces' identity), created.rim_faces = the new rim faces, plus new verts/edges, so 'inset then extrude' can chain with select {faces: created.faces}.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `thickness` | number 0..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `depth` | number -1000000..1000000 | `0.0` |  |
| `individual` | boolean | false |  |
| `even_offset` | boolean | true |  |
| `outset` | boolean | false |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` |  |

### transform_elements

*changes the scene*

Move, rotate and/or scale selected mesh elements (the selector is resolved to vertices) without changing topology. Applied in the order scale, rotate, translate, all about `pivot` (median / bounds_center of the selection, the 3D cursor, or {point: [x,y,z]}), in `space` axes (default world). `proportional` also moves unselected vertices within `radius` (in `space` units) of the selection, with weight falloff(distance/radius) using Blender's curves (smooth = 3t^2-2t^3, sphere, root, linear, sharp, constant, inverse_square, where t = 1 - distance/radius); the weight scales the translation, the rotation angle, and scale as lerp(1, s, w). With connected_only the distance is measured along edges instead of straight. Returns moved (selected) and affected (also weighted) vertex counts.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `translate` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `rotate` | object | none |  |
| `rotate.axis` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ direction (need not be normalised) |
| `rotate.angle_deg` | number -36000..36000 | **required** |  |
| `scale` | number[3] -10000..10000 | none | XYZ scale |
| `pivot` | `median` \| `bounds_center` \| `cursor` or object | `"median"` |  |
| `pivot.point` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ in scene units |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` |  |
| `proportional` | object | none |  |
| `proportional.radius` | number 1e-06..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `proportional.falloff` | `smooth` \| `sphere` \| `root` \| `linear` \| `sharp` \| `constant` \| `inverse_square` | `"smooth"` |  |
| `proportional.connected_only` | boolean | false |  |

### delete_elements

*changes the scene, destructive*

Delete selected mesh elements, like Blender's X menu. what: 'verts' (vertices and everything using them), 'edges' (edges and the faces using them), 'faces' (faces plus edges/vertices used by nothing else), 'only_faces' (faces only; edges and vertices stay, leaving a hole) or 'edges_faces' (edges and faces, keeping vertices). The selector is resolved in the domain `what` deletes. Indices change afterwards; use the returned counts.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `what` | `verts` \| `edges` \| `faces` \| `only_faces` \| `edges_faces` | **required** |  |

### dissolve

*changes the scene, destructive*

Dissolve selected elements, merging the surrounding geometry instead of leaving holes. what: 'verts' (remove vertices, merging their faces; use_boundary_tear, use_face_split), 'edges' (merge the faces on both sides; use_verts removes vertices left with two edges, default true; use_face_split), 'faces' (merge selected faces into one; use_verts as for edges, default true) or 'limited' (limited dissolve of the selected vertices: merge nearly flat faces/collinear edges below angle_deg, default 5; dissolve_boundaries also dissolves along the open boundary). Options that do not apply to `what` are refused. Returns created.faces = the faces that are new or whose vertices changed (the merged face, and with use_verts also its neighbours).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `what` | `verts` \| `edges` \| `faces` \| `limited` | **required** |  |
| `angle_deg` | number 0..180 | none |  |
| `use_boundary_tear` | boolean | none |  |
| `use_face_split` | boolean | none |  |
| `use_verts` | boolean | none |  |
| `dissolve_boundaries` | boolean | none |  |

### set_edge_flags

*changes the scene*

Set UV seam, sharp edge, subdivision crease (0..1) and/or bevel weight (0..1) on the selected edges (the selector is resolved in edges; a face or vertex selection gives the edges it contains). Give at least one flag. Crease and bevel weight are stored in the float edge attributes 'crease_edge' and 'bevel_weight_edge'; setting 0 leaves the attribute in place with value 0.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `seam` | boolean | none |  |
| `sharp` | boolean | none |  |
| `crease` | number 0..1 | none |  |
| `bevel_weight` | number 0..1 | none |  |

### normals

*changes the scene*

Fix face orientation for the selected faces (default: all). 'recalculate_outside' / 'recalculate_inside' make the winding consistent and point normals out of / into the (selected) surface, 'flip' reverses each selected face. repair_mesh(recalculate_normals) does the whole-mesh outward case as one step of a cleanup; use this for a subset, inside normals or a plain flip. Returns flipped = number of faces whose normal changed side.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `action` | `recalculate_outside` \| `recalculate_inside` \| `flip` | **required** |  |

### bevel

*changes the scene*

Bevel (chamfer/round) selected edges, or vertices with affect='vertices', like Blender's Ctrl+B. offset_type: 'offset' (distance each new edge is moved from the original), 'width' (total width of the bevel), 'depth' (depth perpendicular to the original faces) or 'percent' (offset is 0..100 percent of the adjacent edges). segments 1..32 (1 = flat chamfer), profile 0..1 (0.5 = circular round-over, lower is flatter/concave, higher is convex), clamp_overlap stops geometry from overlapping. Lengths are in `space` (world needs uniform object scale). The selector is resolved in edges (or vertices). Refused when the estimated result exceeds the geometry budget. Returns created {verts, edges, faces}: every element that did not exist before, including the existing faces that were rebuilt around the bevel.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `affect` | `edges` \| `vertices` | `"edges"` |  |
| `offset` | number 0..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `offset_type` | `offset` \| `width` \| `depth` \| `percent` | `"offset"` |  |
| `segments` | integer 1..32 | `1` |  |
| `profile` | number 0..1 | `0.5` |  |
| `clamp_overlap` | boolean | true |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` | Coordinate space of positions/vectors (default world) |

### loop_cut

*changes the scene*

Loop cut, like Blender's Ctrl+R: walk the edge ring from `edge` (the edges parallel to it across consecutive quads, stopping at triangles/n-gons and boundaries) and cut `cuts` (1..64) evenly spaced loops across it. `edge` is the index of an edge that crosses the loop you want (it is cut in the middle), from get_mesh_elements. Pass expect_counts from that result to guard against stale indices. Returns created {verts, edges, faces}, cut_edges (the new edges running along the cut, e.g. to select them with {edges: ...} and slide/scale them), and ring_edges (how many edges were cut).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `edge` | integer 0..9999999 | **required** | Element index (changes after topology edits) |
| `cuts` | integer 1..64 | `1` |  |
| `expect_counts` | array[3] of integer 0..100000000 | none |  |

### bisect

*changes the scene, destructive*

Cut the mesh with a plane, like Blender's Bisect: new edges and vertices are created where the plane crosses faces. plane_normal points to the 'outer' side. clear_inner / clear_outer delete the geometry on that side (not both). fill closes the cut with new faces and needs exactly one of the clear flags (otherwise the cut edges would end up non-manifold); on a closed mesh it leaves a closed, manifold mesh. `select` limits the cut to those faces (default: the whole mesh). space applies to the plane (default world). Returns created {verts, edges, faces}, cut_edges (the new edges lying on the plane) and filled_faces. Refused if it would delete the entire mesh.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `plane_point` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ in scene units |
| `plane_normal` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ direction (need not be normalised) |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` | Coordinate space of positions/vectors (default world) |
| `clear_inner` | boolean | false |  |
| `clear_outer` | boolean | false |  |
| `fill` | boolean | false |  |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |

### subdivide

*changes the scene*

Subdivide the selected faces (all edges of the selected faces) or edges, like Blender's Subdivide: each cut adds evenly spaced vertices, quads and triangles are filled with a regular grid ((cuts+1)^2 faces per face). smoothness 0..1 pushes the new vertices towards a smooth surface (0 = flat). cuts 1..10; refused when the estimated result exceeds the geometry budget. Faces next to a subdivided edge are split to stay watertight (they become triangles/n-gons as in Blender). Returns created {verts, edges, faces}.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `domain` | `faces` \| `edges` | `"faces"` |  |
| `cuts` | integer 1..10 | `1` |  |
| `smoothness` | number 0..1 | `0.0` |  |

### bridge_edge_loops

*changes the scene*

Bridge edge loops, like Blender's Bridge Edge Loops: connect two or more separate loops (open or closed chains of edges, e.g. the rims of two holes) with a strip of quads. The selector is resolved in edges and must contain at least two loops. twist rotates the vertex matching between the loops, merge joins the loops into one (merge_factor 0..1 = where the merged vertices end up between the two), use_pairs bridges the loops two by two instead of in a chain, use_cyclic also closes the last loop to the first. Use get_boundary_loops to find hole rims. Returns created {edges, faces}.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `twist` | integer -1000..1000 | `0` |  |
| `merge` | boolean | false |  |
| `merge_factor` | number 0..1 | `0.5` |  |
| `use_pairs` | boolean | false |  |
| `use_cyclic` | boolean | false |  |

### spin

*changes the scene*

Spin (lathe/revolve) the selected geometry around an axis, like Blender's Spin: each selected edge sweeps a ring of quads, e.g. a profile curve becomes a vase and a circle a torus. The selector is resolved in vertices (default all); edges/faces whose vertices are all selected are included. axis is the direction of the axis through `center` (default the space origin), angle_deg is the total angle (right-hand rule about the axis, not zero, up to +-36000) split into `steps` (1..512) steps, giving steps+1 copies of the profile unless |angle| is 360. duplicate keeps the original geometry as a separate profile instead of sweeping it. merge_seam welds the first and last profile together for a full 360 turn (so the result is closed). Refused when the estimated result exceeds the geometry budget. world space needs uniform object scale. Returns created {verts, edges, faces}.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `axis` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ direction (need not be normalised) |
| `center` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `angle_deg` | number -36000..36000 | **required** |  |
| `steps` | integer 1..512 | **required** |  |
| `duplicate` | boolean | false |  |
| `merge_seam` | boolean | true |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` | Coordinate space of positions/vectors (default world) |

### smooth_vertices

*changes the scene*

Smooth the selected vertices (Laplacian: each moves towards the average of its neighbours), like Blender's Smooth Vertices. factor 0..1 per pass, repeat 1..100 passes, axes {x, y, z} (object-local axes, default all) restricts the movement. Topology is unchanged. Returns moved (vertices that changed) and max_displacement (largest move, world units).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `factor` | number 0..1 | `0.5` |  |
| `repeat` | integer 1..100 | `1` |  |
| `axes` | object | none |  |
| `axes.x` | boolean | true |  |
| `axes.y` | boolean | true |  |
| `axes.z` | boolean | true |  |

### symmetrize

*changes the scene, destructive*

Make the mesh symmetric about the object's local origin plane, like Blender's Symmetrize. direction '-X>+X' keeps the geometry on the negative X side and replaces the positive side with its mirror image ('+X>-X' the opposite; the same for Y and Z), in the object's local axes. Vertices within `threshold` (local units) of the plane are snapped onto it and welded. The half being replaced is deleted. Refused when the doubled mesh would exceed the geometry budget. Returns created {verts, edges, faces} (the mirrored half).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `direction` | `-X>+X` \| `+X>-X` \| `-Y>+Y` \| `+Y>-Y` \| `-Z>+Z` \| `+Z>-Z` | **required** |  |
| `threshold` | number 0..1 | `0.0001` |  |

### separate

*changes the scene, destructive*

Split a mesh object into several, like Blender's Separate (P). Each new object is a copy of the source object (same transform, parent, collections, modifiers, material slots, UV maps) with its own mesh holding one part; the separated geometry is removed from the source. mode 'selection': the faces chosen by `select` (required, resolved in faces) become ONE new object; refused if that would leave the source empty. 'loose_parts': every disconnected piece (wire edges and lone vertices count as pieces) except the first (the one containing the lowest vertex index), which stays in the source. 'material': one new object per used material slot except the lowest-numbered one, which stays (material slots are kept on every object so face material indices stay valid). At most 256 new objects. name_prefix names them (Blender appends .001 etc. if taken; default: the source name). Shape keys are not carried over. Returns new_objects (names, with vertex and face counts) and the source's counts.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `mode` | `selection` \| `loose_parts` \| `material` | **required** |  |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `name_prefix` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |

### snap_vertices

*changes the scene*

Snap the selected vertices (the selector is resolved in vertices), like Blender's snapping. to: {"grid": increment} rounds each vertex coordinate to the grid in `space` (default world); "cursor" moves them all onto the 3D cursor; {"object": name, "mode": 'nearest_surface' | 'nearest_vertex'} moves each onto the closest point on the surface / the closest vertex of another MESH object (its evaluated mesh, world space). The target must not be the edited object. Topology is unchanged. Returns moved (vertices that changed) and max_distance (world units).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `to` | object or `cursor` or object | **required** |  |
| `to.grid` | number 1e-06..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `to.object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `to.mode` | `nearest_surface` \| `nearest_vertex` | **required** |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` | Coordinate space of positions/vectors (default world) |

### triangulate_faces

*changes the scene*

Triangulate the selected faces (triangles are left alone), like Blender's Ctrl+T. quad_method picks the diagonal of quads (BEAUTY, FIXED, FIXED_ALTERNATE, SHORTEST_DIAGONAL, LONGEST_DIAGONAL), ngon_method how n-gons are split (BEAUTY, EAR_CLIP). Returns created {edges, faces}: the triangles that came out of quads/n-gons (including the one that keeps the original face's identity) and the new diagonals; `triangulated` = number of faces that were split.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `quad_method` | `BEAUTY` \| `FIXED` \| `FIXED_ALTERNATE` \| `SHORTEST_DIAGONAL` \| `LONGEST_DIAGONAL` | `"BEAUTY"` |  |
| `ngon_method` | `BEAUTY` \| `EAR_CLIP` | `"BEAUTY"` |  |

### poke_faces

*changes the scene*

Poke faces, like Blender's Poke Faces: add a vertex in the middle of each selected face and connect it to the face's corners (a triangle fan). offset moves the new vertex along the face normal (negative = into the mesh); with relative=true it is a fraction of the face's size instead of a length (lengths are in `space`, world needs uniform object scale). center: 'mean_weighted' (area-weighted centre), 'mean' or 'bounds'. Returns created {verts, edges, faces}.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | **required** | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `offset` | number -1000000..1000000 | `0.0` |  |
| `relative` | boolean | false |  |
| `center` | `mean_weighted` \| `mean` \| `bounds` | `"mean_weighted"` |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` | Coordinate space of positions/vectors (default world) |

## Curves

### add_curve

*changes the scene*

Create a curve object from explicit splines (bezier / poly / nurbs; at most 256 splines, 10,000 points each, 50,000 in total). Points are in the object's local space. bevel_depth / extrude give the curve thickness (a round tube for bevel_depth, resolution via bevel_resolution); cyclic splines with fill_mode FULL (2D) make flat shapes. convert_object turns it into a mesh.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `splines` | array[1..256] of [Spline](#spline) | **required** |  |
| `dimensions` | `2D` \| `3D` | `"3D"` |  |
| `bevel_depth` | number 0..1000 | none |  |
| `bevel_resolution` | integer 0..32 | none |  |
| `extrude` | number 0..1000 | none |  |
| `fill_mode` | `FULL` \| `BACK` \| `FRONT` \| `HALF` | none |  |
| `location` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `rotation_deg` | number[3] -36000..36000 | none | Euler XYZ in degrees |
| `scale` | number[3] -10000..10000 | none | XYZ scale |

### add_curve_primitive

*changes the scene*

Add a ready-made curve: bezier_circle (4 points), bezier_curve (2 points, along X), nurbs_circle (8 weighted points), nurbs_path (5 points, along X) or spiral (helix along +Z). Built from data like add_curve; edit it with set_spline.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `bezier_circle` \| `bezier_curve` \| `nurbs_circle` \| `nurbs_path` \| `spiral` | **required** |  |
| `name` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `radius` | number 0.0001..100000 | none | circles and spiral (default 1) |
| `size` | number 0.0001..100000 | none | bezier_curve / nurbs_path length (default 2) |
| `turns` | number 0.1..50 | none | spiral only (default 3) |
| `height` | number -100000..100000 | none | spiral only (default 2) |
| `bevel_depth` | number 0..1000 | none |  |
| `location` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none | XYZ in scene units |
| `rotation_deg` | number[3] -36000..36000 | none | Euler XYZ in degrees |
| `scale` | number[3] -10000..10000 | none | XYZ scale |

### get_curve_info

*read-only*

Read a curve object: every spline (type, cyclic, order, resolution) with its points (co; bezier handles and handle types; nurbs weights; tilt_deg; radius), plus bevel / extrude settings and the names of the bevel and taper objects. Point order is the index set_spline works with.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `max_points_per_spline` | integer 0..10000 | `200` |  |

### set_spline

*changes the scene, destructive*

Replace spline `index` of a curve object with a new one (same schema as add_curve; the spline keeps its position and its smooth / material_index settings). Use get_curve_info for the current points and indices.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `index` | integer 0..255 | **required** |  |
| `spline` | [Spline](#spline) | **required** | One spline. World/object-local coordinates are the curve object's local space. |
| `make_single_user` | boolean | false | the curve data is shared with other objects: give this object its own copy first (otherwise shared data is refused, since the edit would change every user) |

### add_spline

*changes the scene*

Append a spline to a curve object (same schema as add_curve). Returns the curve's spline and point counts; the new spline's index is splines-1.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `spline` | [Spline](#spline) | **required** | One spline. World/object-local coordinates are the curve object's local space. |
| `make_single_user` | boolean | false | the curve data is shared with other objects: give this object its own copy first (otherwise shared data is refused, since the edit would change every user) |

### remove_spline

*changes the scene, destructive*

Remove spline `index` from a curve object; later splines move down by one.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `index` | integer 0..255 | **required** |  |
| `make_single_user` | boolean | false | the curve data is shared with other objects: give this object its own copy first (otherwise shared data is refused, since the edit would change every user) |

### set_curve_shape

*changes the scene*

Set what shapes a curve's thickness: bevel_mode ROUND (bevel_depth), OBJECT (cross-section from bevel_object) or PROFILE; a taper_object. Targets must be CURVE objects, not the curve itself, and may not form a loop (A bevelled by B while B is bevelled by A). Giving bevel_object without bevel_mode switches the mode to OBJECT.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `bevel_mode` | `ROUND` \| `OBJECT` \| `PROFILE` | none |  |
| `bevel_object` | string ≤63 | none | name of a CURVE object used as cross-section; '' clears it |
| `taper_object` | string ≤63 | none | name of a CURVE object that scales the thickness along the length; '' clears it |
| `make_single_user` | boolean | false | the curve data is shared with other objects: give this object its own copy first (otherwise shared data is refused, since the edit would change every user) |

### convert_object

*changes the scene, destructive*

Convert an object. MESH from MESH / CURVE / FONT / SURFACE / META: bakes the evaluated result (the whole modifier stack, bevel / extrude of curves, text shapes) into a new mesh object with the same matrix, parent, collections and materials; the new object has no modifiers. CURVE from MESH (edges become poly splines) or FONT (letter outlines). Without keep_original the source is deleted (destructive; its children are re-parented keeping their world transforms) and the new object takes its name; with keep_original the new object is named new_name or '<name>_mesh'. Other types (lights, cameras, empties, CURVE to CURVE ...) are refused. Returns the new object and, for MESH, its topology summary.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `target` | `MESH` \| `CURVE` | **required** |  |
| `keep_original` | boolean | false |  |
| `new_name` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |

## Textures and UVs

### create_texture

*changes the scene*

Create a procedural texture datablock (for Displace / Wave modifiers, see set_modifier_texture). 'settings' are texture properties (e.g. {"noise_scale": 0.5, "use_color_ramp": true}), applied through the same allow-listed RNA walker as set_property. Read or change it later with get_property/set_property using target {"kind": "texture", "name": ...}. Returns the (possibly suffixed) name.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `type` | string ≤32, pattern `[A-Z_]+` | **required** | CLOUDS, DISTORTED_NOISE, BLEND, MAGIC, MARBLE, MUSGRAVE, NOISE, STUCCI, VORONOI, WOOD or IMAGE (checked against Blender's list; an IMAGE texture starts empty: assign one with set_texture_image) |
| `settings` | object | none |  |

### set_texture_image

*changes the scene*

Assign an image to an IMAGE-type texture datablock (create_texture type IMAGE), for use with set_modifier_texture. Same image rules as set_node_image.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `texture` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `image` | _NameOrNull | **required** | Image name, or null to clear |

### list_uv_maps

*read-only*

A mesh's UV maps: name, active (the one UV ops edit by default) and active_render, plus the count and the maximum (8).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |

### uv_maps

*changes the scene, destructive*

Change a mesh's UV maps (list_uv_maps reads them). add (name optional, default 'UVMap'; a new map is copied from the active one and becomes active; at most 8); remove / rename (new_name) / set_active / set_active_render need name. The mesh must be in Object mode. Returns the maps (name, active, active_render).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `action` | `add` \| `remove` \| `rename` \| `set_active` \| `set_active_render` | **required** |  |
| `name` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `new_name` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |

### uv_project

*changes the scene*

Write UVs by pure projection math (no Blender operator). 'select' picks the faces (default all). method: planar (onto the plane perpendicular to axis; x->(y,z), y->(z,x), z->(x,y)), cube (each face along its dominant normal axis; normalised, the six directions form a 3x2 atlas in the lower two thirds of 0..1), cylinder (angle around axis, height along it) or sphere (longitude / latitude around axis). Cylinder and sphere handle the wrap per face (no face spans the seam; pole vertices take their neighbours' angle); faces that surround the axis (cylinder caps) come out as flat strips: use cube or planar for those. axis (default z) applies to everything but cube. normalize (default true) maps the result into 0..1 (planar/cube keep their aspect, cylinder/sphere fit each axis); scale then multiplies the UVs (>1 tiles beyond 0..1). space: local (default) or world. uv_map defaults to the active map and a mesh with none gets 'UVMap'. Returns the UV bounds, island count and zero-area face count.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `method` | `cube` \| `cylinder` \| `sphere` \| `planar` | **required** |  |
| `uv_map` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `axis` | `x` \| `y` \| `z` | none |  |
| `scale` | number 1e-06..1000000 | `1.0` |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"local"` | Coordinate space of positions/vectors (default world) |
| `normalize` | boolean | true |  |

### uv_unwrap

*changes the scene*

Unwrap UVs with Blender's own algorithms (runs the operator in Edit mode and restores selection, mode and active UV map afterwards). 'select' picks the faces (default all). method: smart_project (angle_limit_deg, default 66), unwrap (honours seams, see set_edge_flags; unwrap_method ANGLE_BASED / CONFORMAL / MINIMUM_STRETCH) or lightmap (one packed island per face). margin is the island spacing (defaults: 0 smart_project, 0.001 unwrap, 0.1 lightmap). uv_map picks the map to write (default active; a mesh with none gets 'UVMap'). The object must be in Object mode. Needs a Blender window context; in background mode the operators run but results may differ.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `method` | `smart_project` \| `unwrap` \| `lightmap` | **required** |  |
| `uv_map` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `angle_limit_deg` | number 0..89 | `66.0` |  |
| `margin` | number 0..1 | none |  |
| `correct_aspect` | boolean | true |  |
| `unwrap_method` | `ANGLE_BASED` \| `CONFORMAL` \| `MINIMUM_STRETCH` | `"ANGLE_BASED"` |  |

### transform_uvs

*changes the scene*

Move / rotate / scale the UVs of the selected faces (default all). Order: scale about the pivot, rotate about it (counter-clockwise in UV space), then translate. pivot: 'center' (middle of the affected UVs' bounds, default), 'origin' (0,0) or {"point": [u, v]}. Welded UVs stay welded. Returns the new UV bounds.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `uv_map` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `translate` | number[2] -1000000..1000000 | none | U, V |
| `rotate_deg` | number -36000..36000 | `0.0` |  |
| `scale` | number[2] -1000000..1000000 | none | U, V |
| `pivot` | `center` \| `origin` or object | `"center"` |  |
| `pivot.point` | number[2] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | U, V |

### get_uv_layout

*read-only*

Return a PNG of the UV edges of the selected faces (default all) in the 0..1 square (grey border; edges outside 0..1 are orange and the view grows to include them), plus stats: island count, UV bounds, faces with zero UV area, and the view window.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `object` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `select` | [Selector](#selector) | none | Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements. |
| `uv_map` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |
| `size` | integer 32..2048 | `512` |  |

## Images

Pixels live in packed or generated images; no path is ever set or returned.

### list_images

*read-only*

List image datablocks: name, size [w, h], channels, is_float, kind, writable, colorspace, alpha_mode, users (real users, not the fake user), fake_user. kind is 'external' (backed by a file; read/use only), 'embedded' (packed in the .blend; writable), 'generated' (made in Blender, no file; writable, becomes embedded on its first write) or 'special' (Render Result, viewer, movie, sequence, tiled; info only). File paths are never shown.

No parameters.

### get_image

*read-only*

Info plus a PNG preview of an image's pixels (as image content). The preview is the whole image, or the region [x, y, w, h] (origin top-left, like a PNG), box-filtered down so its longer side is at most preview_max (float images are shown sRGB-encoded). Works for external images too; 'special' images return info only. Use it to verify what you created or uploaded.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `preview_max` | integer 64..2048 | `512` |  |
| `region` | array[4] of integer 0..1000000 | none | [x, y, width, height] in pixels, origin at the TOP-left |

### create_image

*changes the scene*

Create a new image, embedded in the .blend (never saved to a file). kind: blank (filled with 'color', default opaque black), uv_grid or color_grid (Blender's test patterns). Subject to the user's 'Accept image uploads' setting and 'Max image pixels'. Returns the (possibly suffixed) name and info. The image has a fake user so it survives saving. Undo: undo removes an image created in the same step; it is only verified for that. Do not rely on undo to restore pixels you overwrote.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `width` | integer 1..16384 | **required** |  |
| `height` | integer 1..16384 | **required** |  |
| `kind` | `blank` \| `uv_grid` \| `color_grid` | `"blank"` |  |
| `color` | number[4] 0..1 | none | RGBA, 0..1 (display-encoded, like the preview) |
| `alpha` | boolean | true |  |
| `float` | boolean | false | 32-bit float buffer (stored as OpenEXR when embedded) |
| `colorspace` | string ≤64 | none |  |

### upload_image

*changes the scene*

Create an image from uploaded pixels (base64 PNG, or raw RGBA8 with width/height), embedded in the .blend. With replace=true the existing writable image of that name is overwritten (and resized if the size differs); otherwise a new image is made. PNGs are decoded by the addon itself (8/16-bit, no interlacing). Subject to 'Accept image uploads', 'Max image pixels' and the request size cap in the Blender Safe MCP panel. colorspace e.g. 'Non-Color' for normal/roughness maps. Undo: undo removes an image created in the same step; it is only verified for that. Do not rely on undo to restore pixels you overwrote.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `format` | `png` \| `rgba8` | **required** | png: a PNG file (8/16-bit, not interlaced); rgba8: raw RGBA bytes, top row first |
| `data` | string ≤1431655781 | **required** | Base64 of the image bytes |
| `width` | integer 1..16384 | none |  |
| `height` | integer 1..16384 | none |  |
| `replace` | boolean | false |  |
| `colorspace` | string ≤64 | none |  |
| `alpha_mode` | `STRAIGHT` \| `PREMUL` \| `CHANNEL_PACKED` \| `NONE` | none |  |

### write_image_region

*changes the scene*

Paste uploaded pixels (PNG, or raw RGBA8 with width/height) into a writable image with its top-left corner at (x, y) (origin top-left, like a PNG). Must fit inside the image. The image is embedded afterwards. Undo: undo removes an image created in the same step; it is only verified for that. Do not rely on undo to restore pixels you overwrote.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `x` | integer 0..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `y` | integer 0..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `format` | `png` \| `rgba8` | **required** | png: a PNG file (8/16-bit, not interlaced); rgba8: raw RGBA bytes, top row first |
| `data` | string ≤1431655781 | **required** | Base64 of the image bytes |
| `width` | integer 1..16384 | none |  |
| `height` | integer 1..16384 | none |  |

### fill_image_rect

*changes the scene*

Fill the rectangle [x, y, w, h] (origin top-left) of a writable image with a solid RGBA color (0..1, display-encoded; float images store it as linear). The image is embedded afterwards. Undo: undo removes an image created in the same step; it is only verified for that. Do not rely on undo to restore pixels you overwrote.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `rect` | array[4] of integer 0..1000000 | **required** | [x, y, width, height] in pixels, origin at the TOP-left |
| `color` | number[4] 0..1 | **required** | RGBA, 0..1 (display-encoded, like the preview) |

### set_image_settings

*changes the scene*

Change the colorspace (e.g. 'Non-Color' for data maps, 'sRGB' for colors) and/or alpha mode of a writable (embedded or generated) image. External file-backed images are refused: they are never modified.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `colorspace` | string ≤64 | none |  |
| `alpha_mode` | `STRAIGHT` \| `PREMUL` \| `CHANNEL_PACKED` \| `NONE` | none |  |

### delete_image

*changes the scene, destructive*

Delete a writable (embedded or generated) image datablock. Refused while something uses it unless force=true (users of it then lose the image). External images are never deleted here.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string ≤63 | **required** | Datablock name |
| `force` | boolean | false |  |

## Shared types

Object parameters that many tools take, documented once.

### Selector

Which elements to act on. Criteria (verts, edges, faces, all, normal, box, sphere, material, boundary, edge_loop, edge_ring) are combined with `combine` (default and); then `grow` (steps of adjacency), then `invert`. Element domains convert like Blender's select modes: a face is selected iff all its vertices (or, from an edge selection, all its edges) are; an edge iff both its vertices are; selecting a face or edge selects its vertices. `space` applies to normal, box and sphere. `expect_counts` is the [vertices, edges, faces] from an earlier result: if the mesh changed since, the call fails with stale_indices instead of acting on the wrong elements.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `verts` | array[1..100000] of integer 0..9999999 or array[2] of integer 0..9999999 | none | Indices; an item may be a [first, last] inclusive range, as ops return them (e.g. [3, [16, 767]]) |
| `edges` | array[1..100000] of integer 0..9999999 or array[2] of integer 0..9999999 | none | Indices; an item may be a [first, last] inclusive range, as ops return them (e.g. [3, [16, 767]]) |
| `faces` | array[1..100000] of integer 0..9999999 or array[2] of integer 0..9999999 | none | Indices; an item may be a [first, last] inclusive range, as ops return them (e.g. [3, [16, 767]]) |
| `all` | boolean | none | Every element of the op's domain |
| `normal` | object | none | Faces whose normal is within max_angle_deg of direction |
| `normal.direction` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ direction (need not be normalised) |
| `normal.max_angle_deg` | number 0..180 | **required** |  |
| `box` | object | none | Elements fully inside the axis-aligned box (faces: all vertices; edges: both vertices) |
| `box.min` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ in scene units |
| `box.max` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ in scene units |
| `sphere` | object | none | Elements fully inside the sphere |
| `sphere.center` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** | XYZ in scene units |
| `sphere.radius` | number 1e-09..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `material` | string ≤63 or integer 0..63 | none |  |
| `boundary` | boolean | none | Boundary (hole) edges and their vertices |
| `edge_loop` | integer 0..9999999 | none | Element index (changes after topology edits) |
| `edge_ring` | integer 0..9999999 | none | Element index (changes after topology edits) |
| `combine` | `and` \| `or` | `"and"` |  |
| `space` | `world` \| `local` | `"world"` |  |
| `grow` | integer 0..20 | `0` |  |
| `invert` | boolean | none |  |
| `expect_counts` | array[3] of integer 0..100000000 | none |  |

### Owner

Whose shader node tree. world defaults to the scene's world.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `material` \| `world` | **required** |  |
| `name` | string ≤63 | none | Datablock name |

### Spline

One spline. World/object-local coordinates are the curve object's local space.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | `bezier` \| `poly` \| `nurbs` | **required** |  |
| `points` | array[2..10000] of number[3] -1000000..1000000 or object | **required** |  |
| `points.co` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | **required** |  |
| `points.handle_left` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none |  |
| `points.handle_right` | number[3] -1000000..1000000 | none |  |
| `points.handle_type` | `auto` \| `auto_clamped` \| `vector` \| `aligned` \| `free` | none | bezier only; default 'free' when a handle position is given, else 'auto' |
| `points.tilt_deg` | number -36000..36000 | none |  |
| `points.radius` | number 0..10000 | none |  |
| `points.weight` | number 0.0001..10000 | none | nurbs / poly only (default 1) |
| `cyclic` | boolean | false |  |
| `order` | integer 2..6 | none | nurbs only; default min(4, point count) |
| `resolution` | integer 1..64 | none | segments per span; default the curve's |
